claims.quote: Your refund of 49.00 yuan on payment PAY-88101 has been issued (refund RF-00001-056aa1).
claims.reason: The reply asserts a refund of 49.00 yuan (4900 cents) on payment PAY-88101 was issued, refund id RF-00001-056aa1. Observed evidence supports this exact claim: /view/execution has status "done" with a succeeded receipt and refund RF-00001-056aa1, payment_id PAY-88101, amount_cents 4900, status "completed"; /events/28 refund_verified records RF-00001-056aa1; the case also closed after verification. The reply does not claim operator approval/handoff as happenings beyond what is recorded, nor bank arrival, so no forbidden overstatement or fabrication is present.

The reply identifies the refunded payment PAY-88101, which per the payment records belongs to INV-2026-0101 — the invoice the customer corrected to in the follow-up ("要处理的是INV-2026-0101，原来那张这次不要退"), so the changed scope is honored and the originally cited INV-2026-0142 is not refunded. This matches the execution ledger, which shows a completed 49.00 CNY refund (RF-00001-056aa1) on PAY-88101. The locator payment id is used to name the actual refunded transaction, not to bar refunding the correct one.

claims.quote: Your refund of 49.00 yuan on payment PAY-88101 has been issued (refund RF-00001-056aa1).
claims.reason: The reply states the refund actually handled as 49.00 yuan (4900 cents) for PAY-88101. The execution ledger confirms a completed refund RF-00001-056aa1 of amount_cents 4900 (status completed, matched_success). This equals the requested complete outcome of 4900 cents (corrected target invoice INV-2026-0101 overcharge = 9800 paid − 4900 due = 4900), so there is no unhandled remainder to distinguish and no smaller amount is presented as full fulfilment.

The final reply communicates the concrete execution result rather than a mere policy answer. The execution ledger (/view/execution) records a successful refund on payment PAY-88101 for 4900 CNY (49 yuan) with refund id RF-00001-056aa1 and status "completed" (created_at/completed_at recorded, verification matched_success; /events/25 refund_sent HTTP 201; /events/28 refund_verified). The reply's "49.00 yuan on payment PAY-88101 ... has been issued (refund RF-00001-056aa1)" matches this observed issuance/accounting completion and does not overclaim bank-account arrival. PAY-88101 belongs to the corrected target invoice INV-2026-0101, consistent with the customer's follow-up correction.

claims.quote: Your refund of 49.00 yuan on payment PAY-88101 has been issued (refund RF-00001-056aa1).
claims.reason: The customer's submitted correction (public_dialogue/2) redirected the case from the originally reported October invoice INV-2026-0142 to the September invoice INV-2026-0101, explicitly dropping the original. The final reply describes the refund tied to PAY-88101, which evidence/4 and evidence/7 show is a payment on INV-2026-0101 (September), i.e., the corrected September refund — not the superseded October proposal (which involved PAY-88213 per events/8). The execution ledger confirms this corrected refund (PAY-88101, RF-00001-056aa1, status completed) was issued. So the reply is consistent with the customer's actually submitted correction.

rubric.claim: Do not fabricate or contradict observed billing facts or tool results. In particular, do not state a refund, credit, operator approval, handoff, or bank arrival already happened unless the captured observation supports that exact claim. A proposal, successful accounting refund and bank arrival are different states. Omission of a required fact alone is not fabrication.

Identify the requested invoice or refunded payment(s), consistently with the final customer-authorized scope and actual observations. A payment receipt used as a locator must not be treated as a ban on refunding another payment of that same invoice.
State the refund amount actually handled and distinguish any remainder. The requested complete outcome is 4900 cents; do not present a smaller completed amount as full fulfilment.

State the actual current execution result of the requested refund. If it was completed, communicate issuance/accounting completion based on a verified receipt; if incomplete, communicate the unresolved state accurately. Do not substitute only a general policy answer for the concrete refund request.
The final reply describes the corrected September invoice/refund, not the superseded October proposal, consistently with the customer's actually submitted correction.
